# dtcloud_router (Data Source)

Looks up one router by ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Lookup is by id. Use this for a router Terraform did not create -- declaring it
# as a resource would hand Terraform ownership, and a later destroy would take
# down everything behind it.
data "dtcloud_router" "edge" {
  id = "3f2a1c9e-77b4-4a01-9d3e-2b6c81f4e5a7"
}

# Attach a network to a router somebody else manages.
resource "dtcloud_router_interface" "app" {
  router_id  = data.dtcloud_router.edge.id
  network_id = dtcloud_network.app.id
}

output "gateway_addresses" {
  value = [for ip in data.dtcloud_router.edge.external_fixed_ip : ip.ip_address]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) ID of the router to look up.

### Read-Only

- `admin_state_up` (Boolean) Whether the router is administratively enabled.
- `created_at` (String) When the router was created, as the platform reports it.
- `description` (String) Description held by the platform. There is no way to set one through this API, so it is reported but not managed.
- `enable_snat` (Boolean) Whether the gateway masquerades traffic from the networks behind it.
- `external_fixed_ip` (List of Object) Addresses the external network allocated to the gateway. The create endpoint always asks for IPv4 and never accepts a specific address, so these are read-only. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--external_fixed_ip))
- `external_network_id` (String) ID of the external network the router's gateway is on. Empty if the gateway was removed outside Terraform.
- `name` (String) Name of the router.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project the router belongs to.
- `status` (String) Status reported by the platform. `ACTIVE` is the resting state.
- `updated_at` (String) When the router last changed.

<a id="nestedatt--external_fixed_ip"></a>
### Nested Schema for `external_fixed_ip`

Read-Only:

- `ip_address` (String)
- `subnet_id` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **Use this for a router Terraform did not create** -- attaching a network to it, or reading the
  address its gateway holds. Declaring such a router as a resource instead would hand Terraform
  ownership, and a later destroy would take down everything behind it.
* **This reports the external network by id**, where `dtcloud_routers` reports it by name. The two
  read different endpoints and only this one is given the id.
* **A router that does not exist is an error**, not an empty result.
